common_name: Ever Midnight Agapanthus (Compact Early-Blooming Dark Blue Reblooming Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Ever Midnight is a semi-dwarf Southern Living Plant Collection selection that blooms earlier than standard agapanthus and reblooms through the season.

directions: Ever Midnight is a semi-dwarf agapanthus bred to flower earlier in the season than older types and then send up repeated flush of spikes carrying deep navy-blue flower clusters through summer. Its compact eighteen-to-twenty-inch stature keeps it tidy in mixed borders and large containers without staking. Grow in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, water moderately through the growing season, and remove spent stalks at the base to push the next round of bloom. It tolerates heat and brief dry spells once established, typical of the semi-dwarf reblooming agapanthus bred for southern landscapes.

common_name: Ever Star Agapanthus (Compact Bicolor Blue-and-White Reblooming Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Ever Star is a compact bicolor Southern Living Plant Collection selection that blooms early and repeats through summer.

directions: Ever Star carries large globes of two-toned flowers, each bloom opening blue at the petal base and fading to white at the tips, held on sturdy two-and-a-half-foot stems above a compact mounding clump. It flowers earlier than many agapanthus and continues to push new spikes into summer, making it useful for containers, border fronts, and cut arrangements. Site it in full sun to part sun in well-drained soil, water moderately, and cut spent stalks to the base to encourage continued flowering. Established clumps are drought tolerant and largely untroubled by pests or disease.

common_name: Princess Theresa Alstroemeria (Dwarf Pale Pink Peruvian Lily with Crimson-Streaked Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Princess Theresa is a dwarf, non-staking member of the Princess Lilies series bred by Van Staaveren.

directions: Princess Theresa is an extremely dwarf Princess Lilies selection that needs no staking, producing funnel-shaped flowers in a pale sugary pink with the upper petals washed yellow-pink and streaked dark crimson, from summer into autumn. Its compact ten-to-fourteen-inch habit and long-lasting blooms suit container plantings, border edges, and cut-flower use alike. Grow in full sun to light afternoon shade in rich, well-drained soil, keep moisture moderate and consistent, and pull rather than cut spent stems at the base to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Little Miss Isabel Alstroemeria (Dwarf Red and Yellow Peruvian Lily with Black-Striped Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Miss Isabel is a dwarf selection from the Little Miss series bred by Robert Goemans.

directions: Little Miss Isabel is a bushy dwarf Alstroemeria bearing red flowers with a yellow base and bold black stripes marking the inner tepals, held on compact stems well below knee height. Flower spikes persist for four to six weeks, making it a long-blooming choice for patio containers and border fronts. Grow in full sun in rich, well-drained soil with moderate, consistent moisture, and pull rather than cut spent stems at the base to stimulate fresh flowering shoots. Like other Little Miss selections, it stays compact without staking or pinching.

common_name: Little Miss Vanessa Alstroemeria (Dwarf Orange-Red Peruvian Lily with Brown-Speckled Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Little Miss Vanessa is a dwarf, clump-forming selection bred by Wulfinghoff.

directions: Little Miss Vanessa forms a compact, clump-forming perennial about ten inches tall, with lance-shaped green leaves and clusters of light orange-red, funnel-shaped flowers marked with dark brown speckles over a yellow throat in summer and autumn. Its low, tidy habit suits patio pots and small border fronts where taller Alstroemeria would overwhelm the space. Grow in full sun to light afternoon shade in rich, well-drained soil, keep moisture moderate and even, and pull spent stems from the base rather than cutting them to encourage repeat flowering.

common_name: Little Miss Roselind Alstroemeria (Dwarf Red and Yellow Striped Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Miss Roselind is a dwarf selection from the Little Miss series bred by Robert Goemans, selected in 1998 from a cross involving the 'Aurea' breeding line.

directions: Little Miss Roselind is a bushy dwarf Alstroemeria selected from a cross between an unnamed seedling of the 'Aurea' breeding line and a dwarf Butterfly-type parent, producing red flowers shaded yellow from base to midsection with dark striping on the inner tepals. Its low, bushy habit and long-lasting flower spikes make it well suited to containers and border edges where taller Peruvian lilies would need staking. Grow in full sun in rich, well-drained soil with moderate, even moisture, and pull rather than cut faded stems at the base to keep new flowering shoots coming.
